label.en: Associate Councilor of State and Prince of Yun
Grand Preceptor, Director of the Three Departments, Prince of Liang

sourceDate.text: 宗弼（金初伐宋至皇統八年薨）

people.descriptorSuggestion: Jurchen Ruler and Younger Brother of Shizu

claims.statement: Praised Huandu’s courage and endorsed his judgment.

claims.action: Muzong said: "How bold Huandu is! In my judgment he is entirely right."
claims.sourceText: 穆宗曰：「壯哉歡都，以我所見，正如此爾。」

claims.action: Of Shizu's maternal brothers Muzong was the youngest, and so earned that name.
claims.sourceText: 世祖母弟中穆宗最少，故雲然。

claims.action: Muzong remembered Huandu's counsel and later arranged for Talan's daughter Heluoshen to marry Huandu's son Gushen.
claims.sourceText: 穆宗德歡都言，後以撻懶女曷羅哂妻其子谷神。

claims.action: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.
claims.sourceText: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。

claims.action: Earlier Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, had quarreled over a tribal post and failed to obtain justice. He came in submission to Muzong.
claims.sourceText: 初，耶悔水納喝部撒八之弟曰阿注阿，與人爭部族官，不得直，來歸穆宗。

claims.action: While Muzong was out hunting at dawn, he rallied seven or eight armed men, forced their way into the palace, seized the inner gate, and took Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.
claims.sourceText: 因穆宗晨出獵，糾率七八人操兵入宅，奪據寢門，劫貞惠皇后及家人等。

claims.action: Muzong's heart misgave him and he broke off the hunt.

He met the messenger on the road and reached home at noon. Azu'a told Muzong: "Let the noted bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen band together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou road into Liao, give me gold from the treasury and horses from the stables without stint, and let Huandu escort me to the Liao frontier before he returns."
claims.sourceText: 中途逢告者，日午至，阿注阿謂穆宗曰：「可使系案女直知名官僚相結，送我兄弟親屬由咸州路入遼國，庫金廄馬與我勿惜，歡都亦當送我至遼境，然後還。」

claims.action: He also extorted an oath from Muzong, who yielded to every demand.
claims.sourceText: 而耍穆宗盟，穆宗皆從之。

claims.action: Early in Muzong's reign, his cousins Xilie and Xiebo, together with his elder brothers, murmured dissent: "Those men made themselves lord and minister—what of us?"
claims.sourceText: 穆宗襲位之初，諸父之子習烈、斜缽及諸兄有異言，曰：「君相之位，皆渠輩為之，奈何？」

claims.action: When Muzong came to the throne, every matter touching Liao was placed solely in his hands.
claims.sourceText: 穆宗嗣位，凡圖遼事皆專委之。

claims.action: Huandu dismounted, seized the bridle, and pleaded: "Have you no thought for your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and his wife?"
claims.sourceText: 歡都下馬執轡而諫曰：「獨不念愛弟蒲陽溫與弟婦乎。」

claims.action: Puyangwen is the Jurchen name for "younger brother" in Chinese.
claims.sourceText: 蒲陽溫者，漢語雲幼弟也。

units.zh: 古者太史掌敘邦國之世次，辨其姓氏，別其昭穆，尚失。
units.en: Even in ancient times the Grand Historian who ordered the ages of the realms, sorted clan names, and marked senior from junior lines could not keep the record whole.
units.literal: In antiquity the Grand Historian kept the generations of the states, distinguished their surnames, and separated zhao from mu—and still there were lapses.

units.zh: 金人初起完毅十二部，其後皆以部為氏，史臣記錄有稱「宗室」者，有稱完顏者。
units.en: The Jin first gathered in the twelve Wanyi tribes, then took each tribe as a clan name. Court historians sometimes wrote "Imperial Clan", sometimes Wanyan.
units.literal: When the Jin people first arose in the twelve tribes of Wanyi, afterward all took their tribe as surname; in the historians' records some are called "Imperial Clan", some Wanyan.

units.zh: 稱完顏者亦有二焉，有同姓完顏，蓋疏族，若石土門、迪古乃是也；
units.en: "Wanyan" itself split two ways: same-surname Wanyan were really distant kin, men like Shitumen and Digunai;
units.literal: Those called Wanyan also fall into two kinds: same-surname Wanyan, who were in fact collateral kin—Shitumen and Digunai are examples;

units.zh: 有異姓完顏，蓋部人，若歡都是也。
units.en: different-surname Wanyan were really tribesmen, men like Huandu.
units.literal: and different-surname Wanyan, who were in fact men of the tribe—Huandu is an example.

units.zh: 大定以前稱「宗室」，明昌以後避睿宗諱稱「內族」，其實一而已，書名不書氏，其制如此。
units.en: Before Dading they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong, "Inner Kin"—the same group in fact. Registers record personal names, not clan names; that was the rule.
units.literal: Before the Dading era they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong they were called "Inner Kin"—in substance one and the same. The annals give personal names, not clan names; such was the rule.

units.zh: 宣宗詔宗室皆稱完顏，不復識別焉。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong ordered that all imperial kin take the name Wanyan, and the old distinctions ceased.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed that all of the imperial clan should be called Wanyan, and no further distinction was made.

units.zh: 大定、泰和之間，袒免以上親皆有屬籍，以敘授官，大功以上，薨卒輟朝，親親之道行焉。
units.en: From Dading through Taihe, relatives within tan-mian degree and nearer were entered in the clan rolls and ranked for appointment; when one within da-gong degree or nearer died, court paused in mourning—kinship was honored in deed.
units.literal: Between Dading and Taihe, kin within the degree of tan-mian mourning and closer all had household registers, by which offices were assigned; for kin within the degree of da-gong mourning and closer, death halted court audiences—the way of cherishing kin was practiced.

units.zh: 貞祐以後，譜牒散失，大概僅存，不可殫悉，今掇其可次第者著於篇。
units.en: After Zhenyou the pedigree books were lost; a broken outline alone remains, too fragmentary to exhaust. Here I collect what can still be sequenced and place it in these pages.
units.literal: After Zhenyou the genealogical registers were scattered and lost; only a rough outline survives, and it cannot be set forth in full. Now I gather what can be ordered by generation and set it down in this chapter.

units.zh: 其上無所系、下無所承者，不能盡錄也。
units.en: Lines that attach to nothing above and hand down to nothing below cannot be entered in full.
units.literal: Those with no tie above and no succession below cannot all be recorded.

units.zh: 匡（本名撒速。八世孫。太師、尚書令。）

units.en: Digunai (Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
units.literal: Digunai (Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

units.zh: 婆盧火（安帝五代孫。泰州都統。）
units.en: Boluohuo (fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An; Commander-in-Chief of Taizhou).
units.literal: Boluohuo (fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An; Commander-in-Chief of Taizhou).

units.zh: 胡特孛山（婆盧火族兄弟。）
杲（本名撒離喝。行臺尚書、左丞相。）
units.en: Gao (born Saliehe; Mobile-Administration Minister of the Secretariat, Left Chancellor).
units.literal: Gao (born Saliehe; Mobile-Administration Minister of the Secretariat, Left Chancellor).

units.zh: 什古（昭祖曾孫。東京留守。）
units.en: Shigu (great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Eastern Capital Defender).
units.literal: Shigu (great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Eastern Capital Defender).

units.zh: 崇成（昭祖玄孫。武軍都指揮使。）
units.en: Chongcheng (great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Commander of the Martial Army).
units.literal: Chongcheng (great-great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Commander of the Martial Army).

units.zh: 冶訶（係出景祖。銀青光祿大夫。）
units.en: Yekhe (line traced to Jing Zu; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
units.literal: Yekhe (line traced to Jing Zu; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

units.en: Guhua (Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army).
units.literal: Guhua (Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army).

units.zh: 阿魯補（係出景祖。行臺左丞相。）
units.en: Alubu (line traced to Jing Zu; Mobile-Administration Left Chancellor).
units.literal: Alubu (line traced to Jing Zu; Mobile-Administration Left Chancellor).

units.en: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).
units.literal: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).

units.zh: 胡八魯（穆宗孫，寧州刺史。）
units.en: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).
units.literal: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).

units.en: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).
units.literal: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).

units.zh: 拔離速（宗室子。元帥左監軍。）
units.en: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).
units.literal: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).

units.zh: 銀术可（拔離族子。同中書門下平章事。）
units.en: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
units.literal: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

units.zh: 麻吉（銀术可弟。銀青光祿大夫。）
units.en: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
units.literal: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

units.zh: 宗賢（本名阿魯。太祖從姪。婆速路兵馬都緫管。）
units.en: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).
units.literal: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).

units.zh: 右諸宗室可譜者凡十一族，雖稱系出某帝，而不能世次，不譜於各帝之下，所以慎也。
units.en: Listed at right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.
units.literal: At right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.

units.zh: 又命耶律佛頂以兵護送諸降人于渾河路，以皇弟昂監之，命從便以居。
units.en: Yelü Foding was ordered to escort surrendered peoples along the Hun River route under the emperor's younger brother Ang, who let them settle where convenient.
units.literal: They also ordered Yelü Foding to escort surrendered people with troops on the Hun River route, with the imperial younger brother Ang supervising, ordering them to settle as convenient.

units.zh: 七年，以山西諸部族近西北二邊，且遼主未獲，恐陰相結誘，複命皇弟昂與孛堇稍喝等以兵四千護送，處之嶺東，惟西京民安堵如故，且命昂鎮守上京路。
units.en: In the seventh year, fearing Shanxi tribes near the northwest frontiers might ally with the uncaptured Liao ruler, Ang and Chief Shaohe escorted them east of the mountains with four thousand troops; Western Capital was left undisturbed and Ang garrisoned the Upper Capital route.
units.literal: In the seventh year, because Shanxi tribal groups were near the two northwest frontiers and the Liao ruler had not been captured, fearing secret collusion and enticement, they again ordered the imperial younger brother Ang with Chief Shaohe and others to escort with four thousand troops, placing them east of the mountains; only Western Capital people remained settled as before, and Ang was ordered to guard the Upper Capital route.

units.zh: 既而，上聞昂已過上京，而降人複苦其侵擾多叛亡者，遂命孛堇出裏底往戒諭之，比至，而諸部已叛去。
units.en: Learning that Ang had passed the Upper Capital while harassing surrendered peoples into revolt, the court sent Chief Chulidi to admonish him—but the tribes had already fled by his arrival.
units.literal: Then the emperor heard Ang had passed the Upper Capital, while surrendered people again suffered his harassment and many rebelled and fled; he ordered Chief Chulidi to go admonish them, but by the time he arrived the tribes had already rebelled and left.

units.zh: 皇曾祖太師，威靈震遠，機警絕人，雅善運籌，未嘗衿甲，臨敵愈奮，應變若神。
units.en: The imperial great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, whose authority and majesty shook distant lands and whose alertness surpassed all others, excelled in strategy and never took the field lightly clad in armor; facing the enemy he fought all the harder, adapting to change like a spirit.
units.literal: The imperial great-great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, his authority and majesty shook distant lands, his alertness surpassed other men; he excelled in stratagem and never donned armor lightly; facing the enemy he grew only fiercer, responding to change like a spirit.

units.zh: 大而化之曰'聖'，剛德克就曰'肅'，思慮深遠曰'翼'，一德不懈曰'簡'，請上皇曾祖太師尊諡曰聖肅皇帝，廟號世祖，妣曰翼簡皇后。
units.en: Sheng is for great transformation of all under Heaven, su for firm virtue brought to completion, yi for deep thought and far-reaching consideration, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening—we ask that the imperial great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Shengsu, with the temple name Shizu, and that his consort be titled Empress Yijian.
units.literal: Sheng is for great transformation of all under Heaven, su for firm virtue brought to completion, yi for deep thought and far-reaching consideration, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening—we request the posthumous honorific title Emperor Shengsu for the imperial great-great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, with the temple name Shizu, and Empress Yijian for his consort.

units.zh: 是歲閏十一月，增上祖宗尊諡，始祖景元皇帝曰懿憲景元皇帝，德皇帝曰淵穆玄德皇帝，安皇帝曰和靖慶安皇帝，獻祖定昭皇帝曰純烈定昭皇帝，昭祖成襄皇帝曰武惠成襄皇帝，景祖惠桓皇帝曰英烈惠桓皇帝，世祖聖肅皇帝曰神武聖肅皇帝，肅宗穆憲皇帝曰明睿穆憲皇帝，穆宗孝平皇帝曰章順孝平皇帝，康宗恭簡皇帝曰獻敏恭簡皇帝，太宗文烈皇帝曰體元應運世德昭功哲惠仁聖文烈皇帝，徽宗景宣皇帝曰允恭克讓孝德玄功佑聖景宣皇帝，已上廟號如故。
units.en: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year the court augmented the posthumous titles of the imperial ancestors: Founder Emperor Jingyuan became Emperor Yixian Jingyuan; Emperor De became Emperor Yuanmu Xuande; Emperor An became Emperor Hejing Qing'an; Xianzu Emperor Dingzhao became Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao; Zhaozu Emperor Chengxiang became Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang; Jingzu Emperor Huihuan became Emperor Yinglie Huihuan; Shizu Emperor Shengsu became Emperor Shenwu Shengsu; Suzong Emperor Muxian became Emperor Mingrui Muxian; Muzong Emperor Xiaoping became Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping; Kangzong Emperor Gongjian became Emperor Xianmin Gongjian; Taizong Emperor Wenlie became Emperor Tiyuan Yingyun Shide Zhaogong Zhehui Rensheng Wenlie; Huizong Emperor Jingxuan became Emperor Yungong Kerang Xiaode Xuangong Yousheng Jingxuan—the temple names listed above remained unchanged.
units.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year, augmented honorific titles were conferred upon the imperial ancestors: the Founder Emperor Jingyuan became Emperor Yixian Jingyuan; Emperor De became Emperor Yuanmu Xuande; Emperor An became Emperor Hejing Qing'an; Xianzu Emperor Dingzhao became Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao; Zhaozu Emperor Chengxiang became Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang; Jingzu Emperor Huihuan became Emperor Yinglie Huihuan; Shizu Emperor Shengsu became Emperor Shenwu Shengsu; Suzong Emperor Muxian became Emperor Mingrui Muxian; Muzong Emperor Xiaoping became Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping; Kangzong Emperor Gongjian became Emperor Xianmin Gongjian; Taizong Emperor Wenlie became Emperor Tiyuan Yingyun Shide Zhaogong Zhehui Rensheng Wenlie; Huizong Emperor Jingxuan became Emperor Yungong Kerang Xiaode Xuangong Yousheng Jingxuan—the temple names above remained as before.

units.zh: 仍請以始祖景元皇帝、景祖惠桓皇帝、世祖聖肅皇帝、太祖武元皇帝、太宗文烈皇帝為永永不祧之廟。
units.en: We further ask that the Founder Emperor Jingyuan, Jingzu Emperor Huihuan, Shizu Emperor Shengsu, Taizu Emperor Wuyuan, and Taizong Emperor Wenlie be designated as temples that shall never be removed from the main ancestral line.
units.literal: We further request that the Founder Emperor Jingyuan, Jingzu Emperor Huihuan, Shizu Emperor Shengsu, Taizu Emperor Wuyuan, and Taizong Emperor Wenlie be established as temples never to be displaced from the main line of descent.

units.zh: 丙辰，奉上九代祖妣尊諡廟號，是日百僚上表稱賀。
units.en: On the bingchen day the court presented posthumous titles and temple names for the nine generations of ancestors and consorts; that same day the officials submitted memorials of congratulation.
units.literal: On the bingchen day, posthumous honorific titles and temple names for the nine generations of imperial ancestors and consorts were presented; on that day the hundred officials submitted memorials of congratulation.

units.zh: 愛民長悌曰'恭'，一德不懈曰'簡'，夙夜共事 曰'敬'，小心畏忌曰'僖'，請上皇伯祖太師尊諡曰恭簡皇帝，廟號康宗、妣曰敬僖皇后。
units.en: Gong is for loving the people and long practicing fraternal duty, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening, jing for toiling from dawn to dusk in service, xi for cautious reverence and restraint—we ask that the imperial granduncle, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Gongjian, with the temple name Kangzong, and that his consort be titled Empress Jingxi.
units.literal: Gong is for loving the people and long practicing fraternal duty, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening, jing for toiling from dawn to dusk in service, xi for cautious reverence and restraint—we request the posthumous honorific title Emperor Gongjian for the imperial granduncle, Grand Preceptor, with the temple name Kangzong, and Empress Jingxi for his consort.

units.zh: 又躋楚王宗雄、宗望、宗弼等侍武成王坐，韓信而下降立於廡。
units.en: Prince of Chu Zongxiong, Zongwang, Zongbi, and others were further promoted to attend beside the Martial Accomplished King's seat; from Han Xin downward they stood in the side halls.
units.literal: Further promoted were Prince of Chu Zongxiong, Zongwang, Zongbi, and others to attend beside the Martial Accomplished King's seat; from Han Xin downward they stood in the side halls.

units.zh: 穆宗曰：「壯哉歡都，以我所見，正如此爾。」
units.en: Muzong said: "How bold Huandu is! In my judgment he is entirely right."
units.literal: Muzong said: "How stalwart is Huandu! From what I see, it is exactly so."

units.zh: 歡都下馬執轡而諫曰：「獨不念愛弟蒲陽溫與弟婦乎。」
units.en: Huandu dismounted, seized the bridle, and pleaded: "Have you no thought for your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and his wife?"
units.literal: Huandu dismounted, took the reins, and remonstrated: "Will you not think of your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and your younger brother's wife?"

units.zh: 世祖母弟中穆宗最少，故雲然。
units.en: Of Shizu's maternal brothers Muzong was the youngest, and so earned that name.
units.literal: Among Shizu's maternal younger brothers Muzong was the youngest, and therefore he was so called.

units.zh: 穆宗德歡都言，後以撻懶女曷羅哂妻其子谷神。
units.en: Muzong remembered Huandu's counsel and later arranged for Talan's daughter Heluoshen to marry Huandu's son Gushen.
units.literal: Muzong was grateful for Huandu's words; later he gave Talan's daughter Heluoshen in marriage to Huandu's son Gushen.

units.zh: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。
units.en: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.
units.literal: The Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu all as xiangwen.

units.zh: 初，耶悔水納喝部撒八之弟曰阿注阿，與人爭部族官，不得直，來歸穆宗。
units.en: Earlier Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, had quarreled over a tribal post and failed to obtain justice. He came in submission to Muzong.
units.literal: In the beginning Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Yehui Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, disputed a tribal office with another and did not obtain justice; he came to submit to Muzong.

units.zh: 因穆宗晨出獵，糾率七八人操兵入宅，奪據寢門，劫貞惠皇后及家人等。
units.en: While Muzong was out hunting at dawn, he rallied seven or eight armed men, forced their way into the palace, seized the inner gate, and took Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.
units.literal: Taking advantage of Muzong's morning hunt, he gathered seven or eight men with weapons, entered the residence, seized the sleeping quarters' gate, and held Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.

units.en: Muzong's heart misgave him and he broke off the hunt.
units.literal: Muzong's heart was also stirred, and he ended the hunt.

units.zh: 中途逢告者，日午至，阿注阿謂穆宗曰：「可使系案女直知名官僚相結，送我兄弟親屬由咸州路入遼國，庫金廄馬與我勿惜，歡都亦當送我至遼境，然後還。」
units.en: He met the messenger on the road and reached home at noon. Azu'a told Muzong: "Let the noted bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen band together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou road into Liao, give me gold from the treasury and horses from the stables without stint, and let Huandu escort me to the Liao frontier before he returns."
units.literal: Midway he met the messenger; by noon he arrived. Azu'a said to Muzong: "You may have the well-known bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen join together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou route into Liao territory, give me storehouses of gold and stables of horses without stint, and Huandu must also escort me to the Liao border and then return."

units.zh: 而耍穆宗盟，穆宗皆從之。
units.en: He also extorted an oath from Muzong, who yielded to every demand.
units.literal: He also forced Muzong to swear an oath, and Muzong agreed to everything.

units.zh: 穆宗襲位之初，諸父之子習烈、斜缽及諸兄有異言，曰：「君相之位，皆渠輩為之，奈何？」
units.en: Early in Muzong's reign, his cousins Xilie and Xiebo, together with his elder brothers, murmured dissent: "Those men made themselves lord and minister—what of us?"
units.literal: At the beginning of Muzong's succession, his cousins Xilie and Xiebo, sons of his father's brothers, and his elder brothers had dissenting words, saying: "The positions of lord and minister were all made by them—what then?"

units.zh: 穆宗嗣位，凡圖遼事皆專委之。
units.en: When Muzong came to the throne, every matter touching Liao was placed solely in his hands.
units.literal: When Muzong succeeded, all affairs concerning Liao were entrusted to him alone.

units.zh: 蒲陽溫者，漢語雲幼弟也。
units.en: Puyangwen is the Jurchen name for "younger brother" in Chinese.
